title: Oncall & Incident Response Playbook — Templates, Runbooks, and Comms
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call policies, incident lifecycle, runbook format, postmortem template, rotation guidance, game-day plan, and standard status-page + customer communications. It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and product owners who participate in detection, mitigation, and post-incident follow-up.

Scope:
- All production services and customer-facing endpoints (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private deployment control plane)
- On-call teams: SRE, Serving Runtime, API Platform, Dedicated Ops, and Support escalations

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: SRE (engineering)
- On-call escalation owner: Oncall Rotation Lead (assigned in PagerDuty per quarter)
- Slack incident channel: #incidents (internal)
- PagerDuty schedule: Redwood-Prod-Oncall
- Incident commander (IC): assigned per incident from primary on-call pool

Incident Classification and Priorities

Severity definitions (high level):
1) Sev 1 (P0) — Critical outage: production service unavailable or systemic failure causing customer impact across >20% of traffic or >1 business-critical customer. Requires immediate pager notification and executive awareness.
2) Sev 2 (P1) — Major degradation: throttled errors, sustained latency increases, or partial outage impacting key customers/features. Pager on-call; 15-30 minute response expectation.
3) Sev 3 (P2) — Degraded feature or intermittent errors with limited impact. Alert to SRE/signal channels; not always pageable.
4) Sev 4 (P3) — Minor issues, scheduled maintenance items, or non-urgent bugs. Tracked in backlog.

SLO & thresholds (examples common across services):
- API availability SLO: 99.95% per rolling 30d (error rate >0.05% sustained -> investigate).
- 95th percentile request latency: target < 300ms for small payloads (generation-light).
- Error budget burn alert: >50% burn in 7 days -> operational review.

Incident Lifecycle (step-by-step)
1) Detect: automated alert, user report, or manual discovery. Confirm signal and validate scope.
2) Triage: determine service, severity, and immediate customer impact. Declare incident and open incident channel (#incidents-<id>), create incident ticket in Jira (INC-<id>).
3) Notify / Page: invoke PagerDuty escalation for Sev1/Sev2. Assign Incident Commander (IC).
4) Mitigate: run relevant runbooks to restore service or reduce customer impact. If no runbook exists, perform standard mitigation: route traffic to fallback, scale up capacity, enable degraded-mode feature flags.
5) Communicate: update internal channel, status page, and customers using templates below.
6) Resolve: confirm service stability, close incident ticket, and return system to normal operation.
7) Postmortem: owner prepares a postmortem within 72 hours (draft) and publishes a blameless postmortem within 7 days. Track action items and owners.

Escalation policy (summary):
- Sev1: Page primary oncall immediately. If no acknowledgement in 5 minutes, escalate to secondary. If still unacknowledged after 10 minutes, escalate to staff-level engineer and rotation lead. Contact lists maintained in PagerDuty.
- Sev2: Page primary oncall. If no acknowledgement in 15 minutes, escalate to secondary.
- Sev3: Notify via Slack; on-call reviews during next shift unless flagged urgent.

Runbook Standard (template and best practices)
Every runbook should follow a consistent format; include the following sections:
- Title (service + symptom)
- Scope and impact
- Owner and oncall group
- Symptoms / alert triggers (alert names, thresholds)
- Quick mitigation checklist (1-3 actions to reduce customer impact)
- Diagnostic commands and dashboards
- Rollback and recovery procedures
- Post-incident notes and links

Example runbook: API Gateway 503s (service: api-gateway-prod)
- Owner: API Platform oncall (rotation: Redwood-Prod-Oncall)
- Symptom: >5% 5xx rate across all regions for 10 minutes (Alert: api-gateway-5xx-rate-high)
- Quick mitigation checklist:
  1) Confirm alert in Grafana: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/api-gateway/overview (check 5xx rate and request volume).
  2) Check pods: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=api-gateway
  3) If pods OOM / CrashLoopBackoff: kubectl -n prod describe pod <pod> ; kubectl -n prod logs <pod> --previous
  4) If high CPU or saturating connections: scale deployment: kubectl -n prod scale deploy api-gateway --replicas=<current+2>
  5) If external dependency failing (auth/token service): route traffic to fallback model via routing policy (see routing-runbook).
- Diagnostic queries:
  - Logs (Kibana): service:api-gateway AND status:[500 TO 599] AND timestamp:>=now-15m
  - Metrics (Prometheus): sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (instance)
- Rollback & recovery:
  - If a recent deploy correlates with spikes: rollback to previous revision: kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/api-gateway --to-revision=<n>
  - After rollback: validate with smoke test: curl -fsS https://api.redwood.com/health || exit 1
- Post-incident: add notes to runbook with root cause and update runbook steps if gaps found.

Runbook hygiene rules:
- Keep each runbook < 2 pages when possible and clearly highlight the 3-step mitigation.
- Include exact CLI commands and links to dashboards.
- Mark runbooks as reviewed quarterly by owner.

On-call Rotations and Schedules
- Rotation length: 1 week (Mon 00:00 UTC -> Mon 00:00 UTC) is default for SRE and Platform teams.
- Secondary backup: a second oncall assigned for handover and escalations.
- Handover checklist (at shift start):
  1) Review open incidents and ongoing investigations.
  2) Confirm contact methods and escalation policy are up-to-date.
  3) Note maintenance windows or upcoming game days.
- Vacation & swap policy: swaps should be requested in PagerDuty and recorded in the team calendar; team lead approval required.

Game Days (purpose and example scenarios)
Purpose: Practice incident response, validate runbooks, and exercise cross-team coordination.
Planning checklist:
- Objectives and success criteria (e.g., restore service within 20 min for a Sev1 simulated outage)
- Pre-registered observers and roles (IC, comms, subject-matter experts)
- Runbook & playbook readiness check 48h before
- Post-game-day retro and action items

Example scenario: Region outage (simulate control plane network partition)
- Expected outcomes: team correctly routes traffic to failover region, updates status page within 10 minutes, and completes mitigation within target time.

Postmortem Template (blameless)
Fields to include in Jira postmortem ticket (INC-<id>):
- Title
- Incident date/time
- Severity
- Summary (one-paragraph customer-facing summary)
- Impact (what services/customers affected, duration, scale)
- Timeline (minute-granular timeline of detection -> mitigation -> resolution)
- Root cause analysis (technical cause, contributing factors)
- Corrective actions (short-term mitigations + long-term fixes); include owners and target due dates
- Preventative measures and follow-ups
- Lessons learned and action status
- Link to runbooks, dashboards, and communication artifacts

Postmortem timeline expectations:
- Draft posted within 72 hours (owner assigned by IC)
- Blameless review and publication within 7 days

Status Page & Customer Communication Templates
Recommendations:
- Use a two-track communication approach: Public status page updates + targeted customer emails (for impacted customers).
- Keep messages concise, time-stamped, and avoid speculation. Provide next update ETA when appropriate.

Status page templates (public):
1) Investigating (initial)
- Title: "Investigating: Degraded response from Redwood API"
- Body: "We are investigating reports of degraded responses and elevated error rates for the Redwood API. Our engineers are actively investigating. Impact: Some API requests may fail or experience high latency. Time: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC>. Next update: within 30 minutes or sooner."

2) Identified
- Title: "Identified: Root cause being investigated"
- Body: "We have identified the scope of the issue affecting the API and are working on a mitigation. Impact: <brief>. Mitigation in progress. Time: <timestamp>. Next update: within 30 minutes."

3) Monitoring
- Title: "Monitoring: Mitigation in place"
- Body: "We implemented mitigation steps and are monitoring system stability. Error rates are decreasing but not fully recovered. Time: <timestamp>. Next update: as needed."

4) Resolved
- Title: "Resolved: Service restored"
- Body: "The issue has been resolved and the service is operating normally. Time resolved: <timestamp>. Root cause and postmortem to follow. We apologize for the disruption."

Customer email template (targeted for impacted customers):
- Subject: "Incident report: Service interruption affecting Redwood API ( <brief impact> )"
- Body:
  Hi <Customer Name>,

  We experienced an incident affecting <service> on <date/time UTC> that caused <brief impact>. Our team mitigated the issue at <time UTC> and service has been restored. We will share a detailed postmortem within 7 days. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this email or contact your CSM.

  Regards,
  Redwood Inference Support

Internal comms templates (Slack pinned updates)
- Incident declared: "[INC-<id>] Sev<level> declared on <service>. IC: <name>. Channel: #incidents-<id>. Initial impact: <short summary>."
- After mitigation: "[INC-<id>] Mitigation in place, switching to monitoring. Next: postmortem owner <name>."

Incident Ticketing (minimum fields)
- Title
- Severity
- IC and participants
- Impact summary
- Timeline (with links to logs/dashboards)
- Customer communications (links to status page updates and outbound emails)
- Postmortem link (when available)

Escalation & Oncall Contacts (example flow)
1) Primary oncall (PagerDuty schedule)
2) Secondary oncall (15 min escalation)
3) Staff engineer (30 min escalation)
4) Rotation lead (45 min escalation)
5) Director/VP (when customer SLAs at risk or incident >4 hours)

Operational hygiene and metrics to track
- Mean Time To Acknowledge (MTTA) target: <5 minutes for Sev1; <15 minutes for Sev2
- Mean Time To Mitigate (MTTM) target: <30 minutes for Sev1
- Postmortem completion rate: 100% of Sev1/Sev2 incidents with published postmortem within 7 days
- Action item closure rate: 90% within target dates

Appendices
A) Runbook checklist (quarterly review):
- Owner confirmed
- Commands validated in staging
- Links to dashboards verified
- Test key steps executed during last game day

B) Useful commands & queries (examples)
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=<service>
- kubectl -n prod logs <pod> --since=15m
- curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}
' https://api.redwood.com/health
- Kibana log query: service:<service_name> AND level:ERROR AND timestamp:>=now-15m
- Prometheus (PromQL): increase(http_requests_total{job="<service>",status=~"5.."}[10m])

C) Document maintenance
- This playbook is reviewed quarterly by the Oncall Rotation Lead and SRE manager.
- For major changes (process or contact lists) notify the owner and update PagerDuty schedules and team calendars.
